name: PROMISE
manufacturer: NASA JPL (proposed; built from an existing Mars-rover test vehicle)
best_known_for: Proposed 2026: a JPL Mars-rover test twin, nuclear-powered, sent to the lunar south pole to scout for a Moon base
credit: PROMISE (Polar Rover for Observation, Mapping, and In-Situ Exploration) is a rover NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman proposed on 30 June 2026 for the lunar south pole, within NASA's Moon Base plans: to prospect for resources and scout sites for a base. It would reuse one of JPL's Earth-based Mars-rover test vehicles — most reports name OPTIMISM, the full-scale twin of Perseverance; the Planetary Society describes Curiosity's twin MAGGIE with OPTIMISM parts — and a spare radioisotope power source (MMRTG), so it could keep working through the two-week lunar night. A commercial lander would deliver it. It is a proposal under study, not a funded mission: no launch date, lander or landing site has been named. The Planetary Society estimates $0.7–1.3 billion and sees the early 2030s as more realistic than 2028; Isaacman answered that "if PROMISE costs even 20 percent of your low-end estimate, we simply will not fly it" — its case rests on reusing hardware cheaply.
